candidates.exact_span: The State of New Mexico and Navajo Nation WQS criteria applicable to the warm-water aquatic life designated use are at least 5 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, for dissolved oxygen.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretation of which dissolved oxygen water quality standard applies (State 5 mg/L vs. Navajo Nation 6 mg/L) could change the enforceable numeric limit selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: EPA used the LA-QUAL water quality model, which is a steady-state one-dimensional model which assumes complete mixing within each modeled element, to develop permit parameters for the protection of the State of New Mexico surface water WQS for DO (i.e., 5 mg/L).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether permit DO parameters are understood as derived from the State 5 mg/L criterion versus another applicable standard could change which numeric limit is treated as enforceable for dissolved oxygen.

candidates.exact_span: Primarily based on the City of Farmington Wastewater Treatment Plant’s design flow of 6.67 MGD (0.292 m3/s)) and the receiving water critical flow of 431.3 cfs (278.6 MGD), various BOD5 factors including BOD5 Secondary Treatment Standards were considered and simulated to achieve the DO criterion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether BOD5 limits are tied to design flow, critical low flow, and secondary treatment standards could change which numeric BOD5 limits are deemed applicable or how flow-dependent limits are selected.

candidates.exact_span: A complete characterization of San Juan River (i.e., water quality and hydrodynamic data) was not available. Where data were not available, estimates and assumptions are made.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether missing characterization data leaves limit applicability unresolved (A) versus establishing a documented no-data/assumption state (C) could change how limit pairs and missing-evidence cases are classified.

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington Wastewater Treatment Plant’s design flow is 0.292 m3/sec (6.67 MGD). The discharge location provided in the permit application is located at Latitude 36° 43' 02" N (36.7172), and Longitude 108° 13' 15" W (-108.2208).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretation of which discharge point and design-flow basis governs limit applicability could change which facility/discharge-point limit rows are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: Other effluent parameters provided in the permittee’s application and applied in the model include Ammonia (Avg: 8 mg/L), DO (Avg: 5.63 mg/L), temperature (23 C), Nitrate plus Nitrite Nitrogen (Avg: 20 mg/L), T. Phosphorus (2.9 mg/L) and E. Coli (Avg: 4 MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether these values are treated as enforceable permit limits versus model-input assumptions could change which parameters receive numeric compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The critical low flow of San Juan River receiving stream is approximately 12.213 m3/sec (431.3 ft3/sec).
candidates.computation_change_reason: If discharge limits are interpreted as conditioned on critical low-flow assumptions, a different reading of the applicable flow condition could change which numeric limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: receiving stream average depth of 6 feet (2 meters) were assumed since no data available.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of this as a documented assumption in lieu of measured data versus unresolved missing evidence could change how no-data states are classified for related monitoring expectations.

candidates.exact_span: The model results show no excursion of the receiving stream DO standard of 6 mg/L when the BOD5 limits of 30 mg/l for monthly average and 45 mg/l for 7-day maxima were applied (see graph with 30/45 mg/L BOD5 in Appendix 1; other detail information is available upon request).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states explicit BOD5 numeric limits and monitoring-period types (monthly average, 7-day maxima) and references a 6 mg/L DO standard; different readings could change enforceable limit values (A) and which monitoring periods are treated as required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The model results are based on the assumptions and default values as explained and presented above. Should these conditions change, the model should be updated to provide a more accurate assessment of the water quality within the receiving water body.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether changing conditions render stated limits provisional or leave applicability unresolved could change limit-enforcement outcomes (A) and whether missing or outdated basis is treated as unresolved versus another documented no-data state (C).
